title: Mortara wins Nürburgring Race 2 on a late pit stop
dek: Edoardo Mortara won Sunday's one-hour DTM race for Audi from sixth on the grid, passing pole-sitter Lucas Auer on lap 35 after stopping 11 laps later than the leaders, and moved up to second in the championship.

chapters.title: Wittmann's Saturday sets the stage
text: Marco Wittmann had won Saturday's 40-minute race from pole for BMW Team RMG, with Tom Blomqvist second in a BMW one-two and Jamie Green third for Audi. The result left Wittmann on 155 points, 35 clear of Robert Wickens, who had finished only ninth after starting 13th. Edoardo Mortara, fourth on Saturday, was fourth in the standings on 112.

Sunday's race was longer, a one-hour distance with a compulsory round of pit stops, and DRS was available. That made tyre strategy the likeliest way to upset the order, with four races left in the season after it.

chapters.title: Auer keeps the pole this time
text: A day after losing a pole position to a grid penalty, Lucas Auer made sure of this one. The Mücke Mercedes driver set an early 1m23.064s and then improved to 1m22.728s, and nobody could beat it. Wittmann again finished second, only 0.030 seconds slower, so the front row was the same two cars that had been first and second in Saturday's qualifying.

BMW took four of the top five places. Bruno Spengler waited until late in the session before setting his time, which was good enough for third place, 0.115 seconds off Auer's pace, with Blomqvist and Augusto Farfus behind him. Mortara was sixth, 0.190 seconds off, and was followed by Green and Miguel Molina, so the Audi trio sat on the third and fourth rows. Daniel Juncadella was ninth and Mattias Ekström tenth.
Mercedes' title hope Wickens had another poor session and was only 17th, 0.454 seconds behind Auer. Adrien Tambay set the 21st fastest time but started from the back of the 24-car grid.

chapters.title: Auer leads, di Resta is out at Turn 1
text: Auer got away well from pole and held the inside to keep the lead, with Wittmann and Spengler behind him and Mortara already up to fourth. At the first corner Timo Glock and Paul di Resta collided; Glock fell to the back of the field and had to fight his way forward again, while di Resta's race was over before the end of the first lap, the only retirement.
The leading pair settled into a rhythm. Auer could not pull clear of Wittmann, and for the first part of the race the gap between the two stayed under a second.

chapters.title: Mortara stays out
text: The leaders came in on lap 17, Auer and Wittmann stopping together, and Auer's crew got him back out first. Wittmann briefly found himself behind Spengler, who had stopped a lap earlier, before getting back ahead. Mortara chose a very different plan, staying out for another 11 laps and coming in on lap 28; he rejoined in second place, ahead of Wittmann and with a much fresher set of tyres.

Elsewhere the stops were costly for some. Green left the pits into the path of Gary Paffett and spun the ART Mercedes, and was penalised for the contact. Paffett recovered to seventh. Ekström had also stayed out for a long first stint and changed to fresh tyres only very late, which put him in the hunt for the podium.

chapters.title: Mortara takes the lead on lap 35
text: Mortara was within DRS range of Auer by lap 32, and a first attempt at Turn 1 on the following lap was held off. On lap 35 he went past into the first corner and the Audi simply pulled away, finishing 3.726 seconds ahead of the Mercedes. Auer had led most of the race and took second place.

Wittmann was third, 7.526 seconds behind, and in the last laps he was under pressure from Ekström, who had climbed from tenth to fourth on fresh tyres. Ekström tagged Spengler at Turn 1 on lap 36 and had to give the place back, then passed him again a lap later, and he was in DRS range of Wittmann only on the final lap, finishing 0.323 seconds behind. Nico Müller was fifth, Spengler sixth, Paffett seventh, Blomqvist eighth, Juncadella ninth and Maxime Martin tenth.
Nico Müller set the fastest lap of the race, a 1m24.103s on lap 33.

chapters.title: Wittmann extends his lead, Mortara moves second
text: Mortara called the win a great victory and said the strategy had been perfect: he was able to push the Hankook tyre hard in his second stint and make the pass on Auer. It was his third win of the season and moved him up to second in the drivers' standings, although he admitted it was a shame to have dropped so many points earlier in the year. Auer said he had built a small lead over the BMWs and thought it would be enough, but that he had no answer when Mortara arrived on fresh tyres in a lighter car; he was still happy with second place for the team.

Wittmann said afterwards that his early stop had cost him second place, and he had needed all his tricks to keep Ekström behind him over the final laps, but he was very satisfied with a weekend of a win and a podium. BMW's motorsport chief Jens Marquardt praised the way he kept his nerve in a hard race. Ekström explained that his long first stint on the Hankook tyre, with consistently fast laps, allowed a very late stop to fresh rubber, and that this had almost brought him a podium. Behind them Müller completed three Audis in the top five, which kept the manufacturer's weekend respectable after Green's setback.

The result left Wittmann on 170 points, 33 ahead of Mortara on 137. Wickens, with 120 points, scored only two points over the whole weekend and Green, on 119, finished outside the points after his penalty, so both dropped to third and fourth. Paul di Resta stayed on 100 and Blomqvist, with 93, was sixth. With four races and a maximum of 100 points still to be won, Wittmann was clearly the favourite for his second title, and Mortara looked the last serious challenger. Hankook's motorsport director Manfred Sandbichler agreed that nothing was decided yet, but that Wittmann was in the best position.
The DTM returns in two weeks at the Hungaroring, where the next two races will be held on 24 and 25 September, and the season ends with the traditional finale at Hockenheim on 15 and 16 October.

facts.v: Mortara pitted on lap 28 while Auer and Wittmann stopped on lap 17, and rejoined in second place.
